text: You've finished Platform Fundamentals and this course. Between them you've covered every major domain the real CSA exam tests. This lesson is a map, not new material — it points each exam domain back to the lesson that already taught it, so your remaining review time goes to re-reading, not re-learning.

The CSA exam is a timed, multiple-choice and multiple-select exam from an accredited testing provider, built on ServiceNow's own exam blueprint. That blueprint gets updated per release, so this lesson deliberately won't quote a specific time limit, question count, or passing score. Check ServiceNow's current certification page before you schedule your exam — what won't change release to release is the shape of the content itself, which is exactly what this review covers.

Navigation and UI maps to Platform Fundamentals Chapter 2 — the Application Navigator, Workspaces, and personal settings — plus Chapter 5's lessons on form layout, list views, and filters. User Administration maps straight to this course's own Chapter 1: creating and managing users, groups, roles, role inheritance, and delegated administration. Database Administration maps to Platform Fundamentals Chapters 3 and 4 — tables, base-table extension, the Task table hierarchy, the dictionary, and field types.

Service Catalog maps to this course's Chapter 3 — catalog items, variables and variable sets, catalog UI policies, and record producers. Notifications maps to Chapter 4 — notification records, triggers, email templates, and inbound email actions. Reporting maps to Platform Fundamentals Chapter 7 — building a report, Performance Analytics, and dashboards.

Core Configuration is the seventh domain and spans two chapters: this course's Chapter 2 on access control lists, and Chapter 5 on UI Policies, Data Policies, and Business Rules. The exam's favorite scenario question lives right here — a UI Policy that only hides a field on the form provides no real protection if the question's scenario involves an Import Set or a web service writing to that same field directly. That's exactly the client-side-versus-server-side distinction Lesson 22 built around.

Seven domains, two full courses, and no new material in this lesson — just a focused map from exam blueprint back to specific lesson numbers. Next up: the capstone, where you'll apply every one of these domains to a single real scenario, a small department standing up ServiceNow for the very first time.
